name: Berberine

lead: Berberine is a yellow isoquinoline alkaloid found in plants such as goldenseal, barberry and Oregon grape, long used in traditional medicine. It is sold as a supplement and nicknamed nature's metformin because of its effects on blood glucose.

In fat-loss and looksmaxxing contexts it is used for appetite and metabolic support. Meta-analyses report modest improvements in glucose, lipids and sometimes body weight, though many trials are small and of uneven quality.

paras: Berberine activates AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK), the same cellular energy sensor engaged by metformin, and it inhibits mitochondrial complex I. It also influences hepatic glucose production, lipid metabolism, and gut microbiota. Its oral bioavailability is poor, so much of its action may depend on gut effects.

Gastrointestinal upset such as cramping, diarrhoea and constipation is the most common problem. It inhibits several CYP enzymes and transporters and may interact with drugs including ciclosporin and some diabetes medicines, and it is generally avoided in pregnancy and in newborns because of jaundice concerns. It is sold as a supplement in most countries, so product quality varies.
